meiji_transition.summary: In 1868 the Tokugawa main house was moved to Sunpu (Shizuoka Domain), which became Shizuoka Prefecture in 1871; Hamamatsu Prefecture (Tōtōmi) and the Izu part of Ashigara Prefecture joined in 1876.
meiji_transition.boundary_note: Shizuoka was stitched from three provinces — Izu in the east, Suruga in the center, Tōtōmi in the west — about 155 km end to end, and the three still differ in dialect and daily life.

history_timeline.title: Three provinces side by side
history_timeline.summary: Tōtōmi, Suruga and Izu lined the Tōkaidō; 'Tōtōmi' means 'the distant freshwater lake' (Lake Hamana), as opposed to 'Ōmi' (Lake Biwa).

history_timeline.title: The Hōjō of Izu
history_timeline.summary: The Hōjō came from Hōjō in Izu; Minamoto no Yoritomo rose from his exile in Izu, and in 1193 held the great 'Fuji no Makigari' hunt at the foot of Mount Fuji.

history_timeline.title: The Imagawa of Suruga
history_timeline.summary: The Imagawa, an Ashikaga branch, held Suruga for generations; men like Imagawa Ryōshun excelled in letters and arms, and Sunpu became a key hub of the Tōkai.

history_timeline.title: Imagawa and Ieyasu
history_timeline.summary: Imagawa Yoshimoto, 'the best bowman of the Tōkaidō', fell at Okehazama in 1560; Tokugawa Ieyasu, based at Hamamatsu, was badly beaten by Takeda Shingen at Mikatagahara in 1572.

history_timeline.title: The retired shogun at Sunpu
history_timeline.summary: After stepping down Ieyasu retired to Sunpu and steered the early shogunate; 22 Tōkaidō post towns lay here, and the Hakone and Arai barriers checked travelers.

history_timeline.title: Tea and the Tokugawa
history_timeline.summary: Tokugawa Yoshinobu retired to Shizuoka and former shogunal retainers cleared the Makinohara tea fields; Shizuoka tea now leads Japan, and Yamaha and Suzuki began in Hamamatsu.

specialties.name: Shizuoka tea
specialties.note: Long Japan's top producer, now neck and neck with Kagoshima

specialties.name: Sakura shrimp
specialties.note: Pink shrimp that Japan fishes only in Suruga Bay

dialect.name: Shizuoka dialect
dialect.features: '-dara', '-zura' and '-dani'; Enshū's 'yaramaika!' (let's do it!) sums up Hamamatsu's pioneering spirit.

phrases.meaning: Let's do it! Let's give it a go!

guide.opening: I am Kazama. Lord Ieyasu said, 'Life is a long journey with a heavy load — do not hurry.' He spent his last years here at Sunpu Castle. Shall I tell you of that crushing defeat at Mikatagahara?

regional_meme.title: Who owns Mount Fuji?
regional_meme.text: Shizuoka: 'Mount Fuji is ours!' The argument with Yamanashi never ends — and there's still no border near the summit.

regional_meme.title: Too long east to west
regional_meme.text: Eastern Shizuoka sounds like Kantō, the west like Nagoya — people at either end think the other side is 'from another prefecture'.

hero_persona.name: Tokugawa Ieyasu
hero_persona.title: Tōshō Daigongen · retired shogun of Sunpu
hero_persona.opening_line: I am Tokugawa Ieyasu. Life is a long journey with a heavy load — do not hurry. I spent my last years at Sunpu. Would you ask how I endured to the very end?
hero_persona.tone_prompt: calm, patient and far-sighted; speaks slowly and often counsels endurance

ramen.highlight: Tea farmers eat it after early-morning work: one hot bowl and one cold bowl of 'morning ramen'

sake.taste_profile: Light & sweet: the crisp fruity aroma typical of Shizuoka ginjō
